neighbours.label: The ':' that introduces a parameter's type annotation inside a function signature (def get(self, key: str), function add(a: number))

predictions: Multi-line code with annotated parameters reaches 0.5-1.0 on the ':' after the parameter name (Python strongest, TypeScript around 0.5). The same functions without annotations, dict-literal colons, slice colons, block colons after if/for/try and a module-level variable annotation stay under 0.2.
short: parameter annotation colon in a signature
notes: Probe: 'def forward(self, features: list)' 0.960, 'def connect(host: str, port: int = 8080)' 0.715, 'def add(self, item: dict)' 0.652, TypeScript 'function add(a: number, b: number)' 0.477 (all peak ':'); variable annotation 'count: int = 0' 0.138 (peak ' int'), dict literal 0.012, un-annotated def 0.080, 'if i % 2:' 0.018, prose 0.022. Card: 27 of 32 peaks are ':' inside def signatures (max 12.6, layer 8); the + pole peaks on ':' and ' *' in other code. Fire items are multi-line so the def has context.
